options.title: Airlines fly {fact2} people a year. What do they keep per seat? ✈️
options.first_line: The world's airlines will fly {fact2} passengers this year. So how much of your fare do they actually keep?
options.first_frame: A huge airport departures board flipping to the passenger count over a crowd with suitcases, a jet lifting off through the window behind it.

options.title: Rohan is one of {fact2} flyers this year. What does the airline keep? ✈️
options.first_line: Rohan just paid for one airline seat. So how much of his fare does the airline really keep?
options.first_frame: Rohan at an airline check-in desk handing over his boarding pass, a big jet parked outside the glass with its stairs down.

options.title: {fact2} flyers, and airlines kept half as much. How much per seat? ✈️
options.first_line: Airlines kept half as much of every fare this year as last. So what's left from your seat?
options.first_frame: A jet's cabin seen from the aisle, one seat lit with a price tag hanging off it and a question mark, half the tag torn away.

why: It names the airlines and asks what they keep from your own fare, a question you can only answer by staying, and its departures board with the passenger count reads without sound, while B is about a stranger's ticket and C half-gives the twist and muddles the question.
